The must-sees

8 places Wizzy will tap you for first, each with a story and something to look for.

  1. 01
    Market

    Central Market

    Plečnik designed the colonnaded market halls along the river in the 1930s and 1940s. On Fridays in the warm months the square hosts the Open Kitchen food market.

    Look for

    On the Butchers’ Bridge next to the market, look for Jakov Brdar’s bronze figures from myth and the Bible.

  2. 02
    Bridge · 1901

    Dragon Bridge

    Opened in 1901 to mark Emperor Franz Joseph’s jubilee, it was one of the first reinforced concrete bridges in Europe. Local legend says the dragons wag their tails when a virgin crosses.

  3. 03
    Fortress

    Ljubljana Castle

    The present walls date mostly from the 15th and 16th centuries. Over the years it served as a fortress, a prison and housing; today it is a venue for exhibitions and events.

    Look for

    A funicular climbs to the castle from Krek Square by the market.

  4. 04
    Church · 1706

    Ljubljana Cathedral

    It was completed in 1706 on the site of older churches, after a design inspired by Andrea Pozzo. Its bronze doors were made for Pope John Paul II’s visit in 1996 and show the history of Slovenian Christianity.

    Look for

    Inside, the ceiling and walls are covered with frescoes by the Italian painter Giulio Quaglia.

  5. 05
    Waterfront

    Ljubljanica Embankments

    Plečnik remade the river’s banks with steps, terraces and planted embankments in the interwar years. The work is part of his Ljubljana listed by UNESCO in 2021.

    Look for

    Plečnik’s Cobblers’ Bridge is lined with tall columns, as if it were a room open to the sky.

  6. 06
    Culture · 1941

    National and University Library

    Plečnik designed it in the 1930s, and it was completed in 1941. A dark staircase leads up to a bright reading room, which he meant as a journey from ignorance to light.

    Look for

    The handles on the main door are shaped like horses’ heads.

  7. 07
    Square

    Prešeren Square

    Ivan Zajec’s monument to Slovenia’s national poet was unveiled in 1905. Prešeren is said to gaze across the square toward a relief of Julija Primic, the woman he loved without return.

    Look for

    The salmon-pink church on the square is the Franciscan Church of the Annunciation.

  8. 08
    Bridge · 1932

    Triple Bridge

    The central stone bridge dates from 1842. Jože Plečnik added the two footbridges on either side, with their white balustrades, in the early 1930s.

    Look for

    Stairs lead down from the side footbridges to terraces just above the water.
